items.title: 5 Android phones just as powerful as the iPhone 18 Pro Max in 2026
items.description: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Max is one of the most powerful smartphones available in 2026, but it faces stiff competition from Android manufacturers investing heavily in mobile processing, artificial intelligence, gaming and camera technology. Powered by Apple’s new A20 Pro chip, the iPhone 18 Pro Max delivers improved CPU and graphics performance, alongside enhanced capabilities for running demanding applications and AI-powered features. Apple says the processor delivers up to 40 per cent faster graphics performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. Apple. However, Android manufacturers have also introduced flagship devices powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and newer Extreme Gen 6 processors, as well as MediaTek’s Dimensity 9600 series. These processors bring substantial improvements in computing power, graphics rendering, multitasking and energy efficiency, allowing selected Android smartphones to compete with Apple’s latest flagship. Here are five Android smartphones that offer comparable flagship-level performance to the iPhone 18 Pro Max in 2026. 1. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is arguably one of the strongest Android alternatives to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, particularly for users who want a combination of processing power, advanced photography and artificial intelligence features. The smartphone is powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor, a customised chipset designed to deliver improved CPU, graphics and AI performance. According to Samsung, the processor provides a 39 per cent improvement in neural processing unit performance, supporting faster AI operations and more efficient multitasking. The Galaxy S26 Ultra also features a 6.9-inch display, a 200-megapixel main camera, an improved cooling system and an integrated S Pen. Its combination of high-end hardware, Galaxy AI features and advanced camera capabilities makes it a strong competitor to Apple’s premium smartphone. Samsung has also committed to seven years of software updates, giving the device a longer support lifespan. Android Authority+1 2. OnePlus 15 The OnePlus 15 is another Android flagship capable of competing with Apple’s latest smartphone, particularly in gaming and demanding everyday tasks. It runs on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, featuring the company’s Oryon CPU and Adreno 840 graphics processor. The device comes with up to 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, providing sufficient memory and storage capacity for demanding applications, multitasking and mobile gaming. OnePlus has also equipped the smartphone with a 6.78-inch display supporting refresh rates of up to 165Hz in compatible games. Its 7,300mAh battery, 120W wired charging and 50W wireless charging further strengthen its appeal to users who spend considerable time gaming, streaming and working on their smartphones. With its latest Qualcomm processor and gaming-focused features, the OnePlus 15 is a strong alternative for consumers seeking flagship Android performance. OnePlus+1 3. OPPO Find X10 Pro Max The OPPO Find X10 Pro Max is another premium Android smartphone competing in the high-performance segment. It is powered by MediaTek’s Dimensity 9600 Pro processor, built on a 2nm manufacturing process and designed to handle demanding computing, graphics and artificial intelligence workloads. The processor gives the device the capabilities required to run resource-intensive applications, support advanced mobile gaming and handle multiple tasks simultaneously. The Find X10 Pro Max is particularly relevant in the competition with Apple’s flagship because it demonstrates that Qualcomm is not the only chipset manufacturer producing processors capable of challenging Apple’s mobile silicon. Its combination of high-end processing capabilities and premium smartphone features makes it a notable Android competitor in 2026. Android Authority+2 4. Xiaomi 17 Ultra The Xiaomi 17 Ultra is another smartphone worth considering for consumers looking beyond Apple’s premium devices. The device is powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor, supported by an Adreno 840 GPU designed to deliver high-end graphics performance. It also comes with up to 16GB of RAM, giving users the memory capacity required for demanding applications, multitasking and intensive mobile gaming. Beyond its processing capabilities, the Xiaomi 17 Ultra places considerable emphasis on photography, with its advanced camera system designed to compete with other premium camera smartphones. The combination of Qualcomm’s latest flagship chipset, substantial memory and advanced imaging hardware makes the device a strong contender in the premium Android market. For users who prioritise performance alongside photography, the Xiaomi 17 Ultra offers an appealing alternative to the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Benchmarks and Specs+1 5. REDMAGIC 12 Pro The REDMAGIC 12 Pro completes the list as a smartphone designed primarily for users who demand exceptional gaming performance. The device is powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, one of the latest high-performance mobile chipsets available in 2026. The processor is designed to deliver improvements in CPU performance, graphics rendering and power efficiency, making it suitable for demanding mobile games and other resource-intensive applications. Unlike conventional flagship smartphones, REDMAGIC devices are designed with gaming in mind, incorporating specialised cooling technology to help manage heat during extended gaming sessions. This is particularly important because sustained performance, rather than short bursts of processing power, determines how well a smartphone handles demanding games over longer periods. The REDMAGIC 12 Pro is therefore a strong option for consumers who prioritise gaming and graphics performance when choosing a premium Android smartphone. items.title: Élim CAN 2027 : le Maroc à l’assaut du Niger pour conforter son leadership
items.description: Le Maroc retrouve la compétition ce vendredi 13 novembre face au Niger, à l’occasion de la troisième journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. La rencontre se disputera à 20h00 au Complexe sportif Mohammed V de Casablanca. Leaders du groupe A avec six points, les Lions de l’Atlas ambitionnent de poursuivre leur sans-faute et de prendre une nouvelle option sur la qualification. Après deux journées, le Maroc a parfaitement lancé sa campagne avec deux victoires, contre le Gabon puis le Lesotho, sur le même score de 2-0. La sélection dirigée par Mohamed Ouahbi occupe ainsi seule la première place du groupe avec six points, devant le Gabon et le Niger, qui comptent chacun trois unités. Pour ce double rendez-vous face au Niger, Mohamed Ouahbi a convoqué 26 joueurs, avec notamment le retour de Youssef En-Nesyri. Plusieurs cadres sont toutefois absents en raison de blessures. Dernier forfait en date, Neil El Aynaoui a dû quitter le rassemblement en raison d’une gêne à la cheville. Il a été remplacé par Samir El Mourabet. Malgré ces absences, le sélectionneur dispose d’un groupe mêlant expérience et jeunesse, avec notamment Achraf Hakimi, Nayef Aguerd, Brahim Diaz, Bilal El Khannouss, Reda Belahyane, Ayyoub Bouaddi et Yassir Zabiri. L’objectif sera également de préserver une dynamique défensive solide. Le Maroc n’a toujours pas encaissé le moindre but depuis le début de ces éliminatoires. En face, le Niger arrive avec trois points au compteur. Le Mena a commencé sa campagne par une victoire 2-1 contre le Lesotho avant de s’incliner 2-0 face au Gabon. La sélection est actuellement troisième du groupe, à égalité de points avec le Gabon. Dirigé par Nabil Neghiz, le Niger devra composer avec une situation particulière : faute de disposer d’un stade homologué, il jouera ses deux rencontres face au Maroc sur le sol marocain. Le Mena pourra néanmoins compter sur un effectif largement local, complété par plusieurs joueurs évoluant à l’étranger. Cette première confrontation constitue donc un rendez-vous important pour les deux sélections. Pour le Maroc, une victoire permettrait de conforter sa position en tête du groupe et de prendre un avantage psychologique avant le match retour. Les deux équipes se retrouveront en effet dès le mardi 17 novembre au stade Prince Moulay Abdellah de Rabat, toujours à 20h00. À Casablanca, les Lions de l’Atlas auront donc l’occasion de faire un pas supplémentaire vers la CAN 2027, devant leur public, avec l’ambition de poursuivre leur début de campagne parfait. items.title: US lawmakers summon Nvidia ex-CEO after affair with suspected spy
items.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. “Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote Thursday on X. Scott said he was requesting Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. Nvidia hit gold when the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022 sparked a global rush to develop AI, with its processors — once designed for video game graphics — becoming a crucial ingredient to train and run the technology. – Informal Trump adviser – Nvidia did not give a reason for the departure of Huang, who also gave up his board seat. Huang is Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”. But he said the board had done what it needed: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. Trump, who had stood by Huang throughout the scandal, said former Apple boss Tim Cook should take over. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump said on his Truth Social network, adding that Cook had made Apple “one of the great companies of the world at a fairly short range”. – ‘Going through hell’ – Singapore said Thursday it had barred Alice Huang, a Chinese national, from re-entering the country in February for giving investigators inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed, though she was not investigated for espionage. Nvidia’s board opened a probe on Sunday into reporting that Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort,” while saying it retained confidence in him. When asked Thursday if Jensen should have stepped down, Trump said it would depend. “If the woman was a spy, yes. If the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different,” Trump said in an interview. But Trump said he was confident that Huang will “end up on his feet,” adding: “I spoke to him yesterday. He’s going through hell. What he feels most badly about is his wife and family.” At the heart of the spy allegations is the race between the United States and China for supremacy in an industry widely seen as the next industrial revolution. Key US lawmakers, including Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, called Thursday for answers on what the Trump administration knew about Huang’s ties to a suspected Chinese spy, days before Trump travels to China for a summit. Reports allege the Commerce Department under Secretary Howard Lutnick may have failed to act on suspicions that Megaspeed was helping reroute restricted Nvidia technology to China. Singapore’s home ministry said it had repeatedly sought information from the US Justice Department and FBI on a US server supplier during its Megaspeed probe, but “received limited information or assistance.” On Thursday, Malaysia also said Friday it was investigating a subsidiary of Megaspeed International over the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to other countries. The post US lawmakers summon Nvidia ex-CEO after affair with suspected spy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La géopolitique vue par Mélenchon
items.description: À l’approche de l’élection présidentielle de 2027, Jean-Luc Mélenchon vient de dévoiler son programme. Que défend-il concernant la politique étrangère ? Son projet est présenté comme une réponse à la déstabilisation de l’ordre international. S’il entend rompre avec certaines orientations de l’Union européenne et organiser un retrait progressif de l’OTAN, il réaffirme parallèlement son attachement au multilatéralisme et au rôle des institutions internationales, notamment l’ONU et la Cour pénale internationale. Cette vision se traduit notamment par une volonté de rupture stratégique avec Israël, à travers des sanctions économiques, ainsi que par sa proposition d’un référendum d’autodétermination du Donbass dans le cadre de négociations avec la Russie sur la guerre en Ukraine. Des positions qui soulèvent plusieurs interrogations quant à leur portée et à leur faisabilité. Au-delà des conflits internationaux, son programme aborde également la question de l’avenir institutionnel de la Nouvelle-Calédonie, avec la proposition d’un référendum national ouvrant la voie à une consultation locale sur l’indépendance. Quelle place pour la France dans le monde ? Quelles ruptures stratégiques ce programme implique-t-il réellement ? Mon analyse dans cette vidéo. L’article La géopolitique vue par Mélenchon est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Gaza : Israël accusé d’aggraver la catastrophe humanitaire à l’approche de l’hiver
items.description: a Gaza, les premieres pluies ont submerge les camps de deplaces, transformant les abris de fortune en pieges de boue et d'eau. Mais cette catastrophe n'a rien d'une fatalite meteorologique : les restrictions israeliennes sur l'entree des equipements humanitaires privent des centaines de milliers de Palestiniens de moyens pour se proteger. Dans une enquete publiee le 12 novembre, Middle East Eye rapporte la mort d'Ehab Mohammad Hamad, un nourrisson de six mois, apres l'inondation de la tente familiale. Entre le 6 et le 8 novembre, les intemperies ont frappe un territoire dont les infrastructures ont ete devastees par les bombardements israeliens. Selon l'ONU, plus de 26 000 menages ont signale des degâts, plus de 6 000 abris ont ete detruits et 17 400 endommages. Environ 1,4 million d'habitants vivent encore dans des installations precaires. Israel impose une guerre psychologique Le plus accablant est que les secours existent. Plus de 150 000 tentes achetees par des organisations humanitaires et des etats attendent a l'exterieur de l'enclave, dont quelque 117 000 a El-Arich, en egypte. Pendant ce temps, l'ONU estime qu'il faudrait 121 000 tentes supplementaires pour affronter le froid. L'ecart entre ces stocks et les besoins illustre les consequences concretes des entraves a l'acheminement de l'aide. Bâches, couvertures, equipements de pompage : leur arrivee reste soumise a des restrictions israeliennes, auxquelles s'ajoutent des obstacles logistiques et financiers. Ces blocages pesent d'autant plus lourd que les reseaux d'assainissement ont ete ravages et que les familles n'ont souvent aucun refuge alternatif. Pour les organisations humanitaires, Israel porte une responsabilite majeure dans l'aggravation de cette crise. Les pluies sont naturelles ; laisser des familles affronter l'hiver sans abri adequat, alors que du materiel attend aux frontieres, releve aussi de choix politiques.

items.title: Le Cameroun et l’UNFPA lancent le 9è Programme de coopération économique 2027-2031
items.description: © DR La cérémonie de lancement a eu lieu le 11 novembre 2026 sous la présidence du ministre de l’Economie, de la Planification et de l’Aménagement du territoire Alamine Ousmane Mey et le coordonnateur résident du Système des Nations unies au Cameroun, Issa Sanogo. Le Cameroun et le Fonds des Nations unies pour la population ont lancé mercredi le 9è Programme de coopération Cameroun-UNFPA 2027-2031. Le programme vise à contribuer au développement du capital humain au Cameroun. Il met l’accent sur l’amélioration des services de santé sexuelle et reproductive, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, l’autonomisation des femmes et des jeunes, le renforcement de la production et de l’utilisation des données démographiques dans l’élaboration des politiques publiques. En alignement sur l’Agenda 2030 et l’Agenda 2063, le CPD9 vise à atteindre des performances records sur trois axes : zéro décès maternel évitable, zéro besoin non satisfait en matière de planification familiale ; zéro violence basée sur le genre et pratique néfaste. Le programme est estimé à 69 millions de dollars (40, 917 milliards de FCFA) dont près de 30 millions (17, 790 milliards de FCFA) sont déjà mobilisés par l’UNFPA, le CPD9. Lors de la cérémonie de lancement dudit programme baptisé CPD9, ses orientations stratégiques et son cadre de ressources ont été présentés. De même, il a été question de partager les acquis du programme précédent, de renforcer la mobilisation des administrations, des partenaires techniques et financiers, de la société civile autour du programme. Pour ce qui est du programme CPD8 (2022-2026) en effet, plusieurs acquis sont à relever : augmentation des formations sanitaires offrant des soins obstétricaux néonatals d’urgence de 100 à 273 ; soins et accompagnement à la réinsertion de 337 femmes souffrant de fistules obstétricales ; prise en charge de plus de 210 000 victimes de violences basées sur le genre par 122 espaces sûrs. Cet article Le Cameroun et l’UNFPA lancent le 9è Programme de coopération économique 2027-2031 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Security forces kill 74 terrorists during IBOs in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan: ISPR
items.description: Security forces have killed 74 terrorists during intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) and Balochistan, said a statement by the military’s media wing on Friday. In a breakdown of casualties from operations conducted in KP over the past 48 hours, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said 35 terrorists were killed in Mir Ali, North Waziristan district, while eight others were killed in Orakzai district. “In a determined effort to eliminate terrorist threats and dismantle the khwarij networks, security forces are conducting a series of intelligence-based operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. These operations have been further expanded to the areas of Mir Ali and Orakzai,” said ISPR. Elaborating further, the military’s media wing said that “intense and fierce exchanges of fire” took place, dealing a “significant blow” to the networks operated by the terrorists in the areas. Fitna-al-Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. A large cache of weapons, ammunition and explosives, including homemade explosives and improvised explosive devices (IEDs), was also recovered during sanitisation, the military’s media wing said, adding that the recoveries had thwarted the “nefarious designs” of the terrorists to use the materials in terrorist activities. The ISPR further said that sanitisation operations continue in the areas to “eliminate holed up khwarij ”. President, PM pay tribute to security forces Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to security forces personnel for eliminating terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in Kurram, state-run APP reported. An official statement carried by APP said the prime minister praised the professional expertise and courage of security forces personnel for destroying several terrorist hideouts and recovering a large cache of arms, ammunition and explosives during the operation. He noted that the security forces were working round the clock to foil the “nefarious designs of anti-state elements”. The prime minister reaffirmed that the fight against foreign-sponsored terrorism would continue with full force under the National Action Plan (NAP) until terrorism was eliminated from the country. President Asif Ali Zardari also paid tribute to the security forces for carrying out intelligence-based operations against terrorists. According to a statement issued by the Presidency, the president said the security forces’ continued successes in the fight against terrorism reflected their professional capabilities. “The recovery of weapons, ammunition and explosives from the possession of terrorists demonstrated the effectiveness of the security forces’ action”, he said. He added that the ambitions of “externally sponsored terrorists seeking to undermine Pakistan’s peace and stability will not be allowed to succeed”. IBOs in Balochistan Security forces have killed 31 terrorists since Nov 3 during a “comprehensive intelligence-based area sanitisation operation” against India-backed Fitna al Khawarij and Fitna al Hindustan in the Kurram area of Quetta district, the military’s media wing said. The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. “During the conduct of these intelligence-based operations, multiple terrorist hideouts were effectively engaged and after multiple engagements, thirty one Indian sponsored khwarij were sent to hell. Weapons, ammunition and explosives were also recovered from the Khwariji locations,” said ISPR. “Sanitisation operations are being conducted to eliminate any other India-sponsored terrorist found in the area,” the statement read, adding that a relentless counterterrorism campaign under the vision “Azm-i-Istehkam” will continue at full pace to “wipe out [the] menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”. The country’s security environment continued to show considerable volatility from October 30 to November 5, 2026, with renewed terrorist activity in parts of KP and the former tribal districts, alongside intensified counterterrorism operations and changing patterns of militant violence, according to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS) . Per the latest PICSS Weekly Insight , 49 militant attacks were recorded nationwide during the reporting period, compared with 31 in the preceding week. These incidents resulted in 25 fatalities and 21 injuries. On October 8 , security forces killed nine terrorists in an IBO in North Waziristan, while a day earlier , 18 terrorists were eliminated in separate engagements in KP and Balochistan.

items.title: Asean faces Myanmar dilemma as some members pursue closer ties
items.description: Asean is under increasing pressure at its upcoming summit to ease a five-year ban on Myanmar’s military-backed leaders attending high-level meetings, after Thailand and several other members stepped up engagement despite the country’s ongoing civil war . Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) are set to review their decision to exclude Myanmar when they meet in Manila from Nov 15 to Nov 17. Myanmar has been in turmoil since 2021, when then-military chief Min Aung Hlaing ousted the elected government in a coup, unleashing armed conflict across much of the country that has killed more than 100,000 people. Its political leadership has been barred from Asean summits and foreign ministers’ meetings over its failure to implement the Five-Point Consensus, a peace plan agreed after the coup. But nearly half the bloc’s 11 members have stepped up bilateral engagement since elections in December and January, won overwhelmingly by the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party in the absence of any viable opposition. Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Malaysia have this year welcomed Min Aung Hlaing on official visits. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim pledged in October to work towards Myanmar’s reintegration into the bloc. Thailand is now openly calling for restrictions to be eased. “For Thailand, we believe that the next step is to have the foreign minister of Myanmar participate in the Asean meetings at the level of foreign minister,” Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow told reporters after visiting Myanmar on Thursday. He hoped sufficient progress would allow a decision on Myanmar’s participation by Thailand’s chairmanship in 2028 at the latest. Engaging policymakers would help convey Asean’s concerns directly to decision-makers, he said, while stressing that the decision rested with the bloc’s foreign ministers. Separate diplomatic tracks Analysts say the shifting approaches put pressure on the Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence, inclusive dialogue, humanitarian assistance and mediation by an envoy able to meet all parties. Leaders will issue a negotiated document reviewing its implementation at the upcoming Asean summit, Dominic Xavier Imperial, a spokesperson for the Philippines, said on Friday. “I think the Five-Point Consensus now has been overtaken by events,” said Thitinan Pongsudhirak, a political scientist at Bangkok’s Chulalongkorn University. Implementation has made little headway. Civil war continues, millions remain displaced and efforts to bring the warring parties into dialogue have yet to produce a breakthrough. Aung San Suu Kyi , the country’s civilian leader and a Nobel Peace Prize winner, has been detained since the coup. She was moved to house arrest in April, following the military-engineered election, but while a Red Cross official was allowed to meet her in August, no foreign leader or envoy has been able to despite requests. Thailand has repeatedly offered to facilitate talks between Myanmar’s government and ethnic armed groups along its border. Sihasak said Myanmar had agreed in principle to send a delegation to any talks, but gave no date. Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, Asean’s special envoy, visited Myanmar on a humanitarian mission in October. But the envoy’s role, which changes each year with Asean’s rotating chairmanship, is also under scrutiny. “Myanmar’s been keen to do away with the special envoy entirely,” said a Southeast Asian diplomat who declined to be named, adding that ongoing discussions had also covered appointing a permanent envoy. “But if no consensus on either of these approaches, then the status quo will remain,” the diplomat said. Testing Asean unity Thailand’s assertive engagement reflects the country’s concerns over fighting spilling across its long land border with Myanmar, alongside trade, migrant workers and energy cooperation. But Thitinan said Bangkok’s “calibrated re-engagement” had pressured other capitals to follow suit, leaving Singapore, next year’s chair, to reconcile divergent approaches. “It should not have been a blank cheque; it should not have been an open-ended reception and recognition,” he said, advocating conditions including political prisoner releases, humanitarian access and an end to military airstrikes. Human Rights Watch has urged Asean to maintain restrictions and increase pressure on the military to end abuses and pursue a transition to civilian rule . Warmer bilateral ties do not automatically change Asean policy, however, said Simon Tay, chairman of the Singapore Institute of International Affairs. The consensus remains unless members collectively agree otherwise. “There is room for both good cop and bad cop within Asean, provided these different approaches remain within the 5PC framework,” he said. “Otherwise, Myanmar could simply play one against the other.” Tay advocates interim goals including regular access to Aung San Suu Kyi, reduced violence and humanitarian aid. “Asean can be pragmatic without being premature,” he said. “Political acceptance should follow progress, not precede it.”

items.title: Abductors of FUNAAB graduate, three others demand N500m ransom
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The abductors of a recent graduate of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), Adedoja Hannah, and three other individuals have reportedly demanded a ransom of N500 million for their release. The victims were allegedly kidnapped on Tuesday night when suspected gunmen invaded a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta, Ogun State, where they were working. The development was disclosed by the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of FUNAAB in a statement posted on its official Facebook platform on Thursday, expressing concern over the safety of the victims and appealing to members of the university community and the general public to remain calm. According to the union, Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, was among the four people abducted during the incident. Providing an account of the circumstances surrounding her disappearance, the union stated that Hannah was last seen on Monday, while her telephone has remained unreachable since the reported abduction. The statement partly reads, “The Students’ Union Government wishes to update the FUNAAB community and the general public on the abduction of Adedoja Hannah, a recent graduate of the Department of Agricultural Administration, Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB), alongside three other individuals at a farm along the Akintobi-Alabata axis of Abeokuta. “According to information received, the incident occurred on Tuesday night when suspected kidnappers reportedly invaded the farm where the victims were working. Hannah was last seen on Monday, and her phone has remained unreachable since the incident. “Further information indicates that the abductors have demanded a ransom of ₦500 million for the release of all four victims. This development has understandably heightened concerns over their safety and the circumstances surrounding the incident. “The incident was reported to the appropriate security authorities, and the police have been working on the matter since Tuesday. Security efforts are ongoing, with attention directed towards locating the victims and securing their safe release. “We understand the concern this incident has generated, particularly among residents and members of the university community around the Alabata axis. However, we appeal to everyone to remain calm and allow the relevant authorities to carry out their investigations and response. “It is equally important that information shared publicly is accurate and responsible. Unverified reports and speculation should be avoided, especially where they could interfere with ongoing security efforts. “The Union is deeply concerned about the safety of Hannah and the other victims. Although Hannah is a recent graduate, she remains an important member of the wider FUNAAB community, and we recognise the distress this situation has caused her family, friends and loved ones. “We remain hopeful for the safe and immediate return of all four victims. Anyone with credible information that could assist the security authorities is encouraged to report it through the appropriate channels. “We also appeal to members of the university community and the general public to keep the victims and their families in their thoughts during this difficult period. “The Students’ Union Government will continue to encourage responsible communication as the situation develops”. When contacted, the Ogun State Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, confirmed the abduction. Babaseyi said, “we are on the issue since it happened; rescue operations are in top gear”. The post Abductors of FUNAAB graduate, three others demand N500m ransom appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Financement de la formation professionnelle et technique : Le 3Fpt et l’Ansd dressent un bilan positif
items.description: Le Fonds de financement de la formation professionnelle et technique (3fpt), l’Agence nationale de la statistique et de la démographie (Ansd) ont présenté, jeudi 12 novembre, les résultats d’une évaluation majeure. Entre 2016 et 2024, les investissements consentis ont permis d'accroître considérablement les capacités d'accueil et la qualité des offres de formation. Pour tailler de nouveaux habits adaptés aux ambitions de l’agenda national de transformation « Sénégal 2050 », il fallait d’abord évaluer la garde-robe précédente. C’est par cette métaphore que Soulèye Kane, Directeur général du 3fpt, a résumé l’enjeu de l’atelier de restitution des résultats de l’évaluation du dispositif de financement des établissements de formation professionnelle et technique qui s’est tenu, hier, à Dakar. Conduite par l’Agence nationale de la statistique et de la démographie (Ansd) sur la période 2016-2024, cette étude indépendante vise à mesurer l’impact réel des fonds publics injectés dans le secteur, selon six critères rigoureux que sont la pertinence, la cohérence, l’efficacité, l’efficience, l’impact et la durabilité. Pour le Directeur général de l’Ansd, Abdou Diouf, ces résultats constituent « un précieux outil d’aide à la décision » permettant aux autorités d’avoir une lecture éclairée sur l’efficacité du dispositif et d’orienter les futurs financements. L’évaluation a porté sur les quatre guichets d’intervention du 3fpt au profit des établissements publics. Les chiffres dévoilés par le secrétaire général du ministère de la Formation professionnelle et technique, Mamadou Camara Fall, témoignent d'un bond quantitatif et qualitatif notable. Il y a l’élargissement de l’accès. Sur ce point il y a la construction d'ateliers et la dotation en équipements conformes aux référentiels permettant de créer 4.783 postes de travail supplémentaires (soit une hausse de 207%). Ce qui a induit un accroissement de la capacité d’accueil de 156,6% et d’ouvrir 180 à 186 nouvelles filières. Il y a également, la gouvernance. Sur cet aspect, l’évaluation révèle que 82,6% des établissements ciblés ont élaboré et validé leur plan stratégique, avec un taux de mise en œuvre effective de 98%. L’adaptation des cursus n’a pas été en reste : de nouveaux référentiels de compétences, calqués sur les besoins émergents du marché, ont été élaborés dans 75,17% des cas. Enfin, la qualité pédagogique : 4.227 formateurs et acteurs du secteur ont vu leurs compétences renforcées, affichant un taux de satisfaction de 93,5%. Par ailleurs, les acteurs entendent passer à la vitesse supérieure. « La séquence de 2034 nous convoque à former entre 500.000 et 700.000 techniciens au Sénégal », a rappelé Soulèye Kane, soulignant la nécessité d’éviter toute dispersion financière et de rationaliser les investissements. À cet effet, M. camara a évoqué la suite à donner à cette étude. Pour le secrétaire général, une restitution n’a de sens que si elle éclaire l’action. Il a ainsi appelé à la mise en place d’un suivi rigoureux des recommandations, avec des échéances précises, tout en veillant à la maintenance des équipements acquis et à l'équité dans l’accès aux financements. Samba DIAMANKA

items.title: Burkina : À Ouahigouya, l’insémination artificielle séduit les éleveurs
items.description: Le ministre délégué chargé des Ressources animales, Dr Amadou Dicko, a achevé ce jeudi 12 novembre 2026 une tournée de suivi de la campagne de déparasitage, de vaccination et d'insémination artificielle du cheptel dans la région du Yaadga. Sur place, 278 vaches ont déjà été inséminées sur un objectif régional de 3 000. Si le ministre se félicite des résultats pour les petits ruminants, il reconnaît un rythme « timide » pour les bovins, freiné par la période des récoltes. Débutée le mardi 10 novembre, la tournée du Ministère de l'Agriculture, de l'Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, conduite à travers la Direction générale des services vétérinaires, a d'abord concerné les régions du Nazinon et d'Oubri avant de s'achever dans le Yaadga. Le ministre délégué vaccinant des bovins à Lougouri L'objectif de cette mission était d'apprécier l'évolution des opérations sur le terrain dans le cadre de la campagne 2026-2027, officiellement lancée le 19 septembre dernier. À Souli, dans le secteur 1 de Ouahigouya, les autorités ont pu constater le déroulement de l'insémination artificielle sur des vaches, qui ont également reçu des boucles RFID destinées à faciliter leur identification au sein des troupeaux. Dans cette région, l'ambition est d'inséminer 3 000 bovins. À la date du passage de la délégation, 278 vaches avaient déjà été inséminées. À Gourouga, dans le secteur 15, la délégation a suivi une opération de vaccination des petits ruminants, accueillie par des populations fortement mobilisées, dans une ambiance rythmée par des chants et des applaudissements. À Lougouri, dans la commune de Oula, des bovins ont également bénéficié de la vaccination. Dr Amadou Dicko montrant sa satisfaction de la tournée en général Au terme de la tournée, Dr Amadou Dicko s'est dit satisfait du déroulement de la campagne dans les régions visitées. « Le déroulement est très satisfaisant dans l'ensemble des régions pour ce qui concerne la peste des petits ruminants », a-t-il indiqué. Dr Dicko a toutefois relevé un rythme relativement timide de la vaccination des bovins, en raison de la période des récoltes. « Les agents ont déjà de très bons taux de vaccination, mais comme nous sommes en période de récoltes, pour les bovins, le rythme est assez timide. Nous espérons atteindre, à la fin de cette campagne, des taux très satisfaisants en matière de vaccination et d'insémination des animaux », a-t-il expliqué. Selon le ministre délégué, cette campagne constitue la quatrième opération de vaccination d'envergure menée dans cette dynamique. À terme, les autorités ambitionnent de contrôler certaines maladies animales en réduisant leur prévalence et d'en éradiquer d'autres à l'horizon 2030. Pour y parvenir, l'État subventionne plusieurs vaccins, tandis que d'autres sont administrés gratuitement. Une insémination artificielle réalisée par l'équipe en présence des autorités Dr Amadou Dicko a également évoqué les investissements engagés dans la santé animale, notamment la construction d'une unité nationale de fabrication de vaccins pour animaux à Samandéni, ainsi que la mise en place de la Centrale d'approvisionnement en médicaments vétérinaires et de ses représentations. Il a par ailleurs annoncé la tenue d'un atelier de bilan à mi-parcours le 27 novembre prochain, afin de formuler des recommandations pour l'atteinte des objectifs fixés, avec l'ambition d'obtenir les meilleurs résultats possibles d'ici février 2027. Sur le terrain, les opérations ont aussi été saluées par les bénéficiaires. Boureima Kindo, éleveur dans la région, a exprimé sa reconnaissance envers les autorités pour les actions engagées en faveur de la santé animale. « Quand on fait l'élevage, les animaux rencontrent souvent des maladies qui peuvent même décimer tout le troupeau. Mais grâce à la vision du Chef de l'État, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, ainsi qu'au ministre d'État, le commandant Ismaël Sombié, et à toute son équipe, nous sommes sur le chemin d'éradiquer ce fléau », a-t-il déclaré. Pour M. Kindo, la lutte contre les maladies animales revêt une importance particulière pour les communautés, tant l'élevage occupe une place essentielle dans leur vie sociale et économique. « Dans notre société, l'animal est associé à tout événement, qu'il soit heureux ou malheureux », a-t-il déclaré. Boureima Kindo appréciant les efforts du gouvernement à les accompagner Boureima Kindo a également mis en avant les avantages de l'insémination artificielle, qui permet notamment d'améliorer les caractéristiques génétiques du cheptel grâce à l'utilisation de semences issues d'autres races. « Non seulement avant l'insémination, la vache bénéficiaire est totalement traitée de tout maux. Également, les semences inséminées sont d'une autre race dont notre vache va mettre bas d'un métisse, et cette joie est inexplicable car sans cette pratique où nous allions trouver ce bovin pour féconder notre vache », s'est-il réjoui. Pour la vaccination des petits ruminants, M. Kindo a salué la gratuité qui va permettre à tous les éleveurs de faire vacciner leurs animaux, et a assuré de l'engagement dont ils font preuve pour l'effectivité de la campagne. Un bovin vacciné En marge du suivi de la campagne, la délégation a visité un magasin de conservation de pailles d'arachide et de haricot dans le Yaadga, ainsi que deux sites de culture de Maralfalfa dans les régions du Nazinon et du Yaadga. Ces visites ont été l'occasion d'encourager les producteurs à poursuivre leurs efforts pour développer ces cultures fourragères et améliorer l'alimentation du bétail. Pour rappel, la campagne 2026-2027 vise notamment à lutter contre les principales maladies animales, dont la péripneumonie contagieuse bovine, la peste des petits ruminants et la maladie de Newcastle, afin de préserver le patrimoine animalier national et de renforcer la contribution de l'élevage à la sécurité alimentaire et à l'économie du Burkina Faso. ‘Years of injustice’ fuel northern Nigeria violence, says bandit leader
items.description: Decades of discrimination and extortion against Fulani herders are stoking the growing violence in northern Nigeria — unrest which will only swell until authorities tame the rampant corruption in the region, a bandit kingpin told AFP in a rare interview. Northwest and central Nigeria have for years been terrorised by gangs known locally as “bandits”, who raid villages, rustle cattle, conduct kidnappings and impose “taxes” on farmers and miners. The interview with one such gang leader came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, in a piece published Thursday, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and AFP northern Nigeria reporter Aminu Abubakar. “Years of injustices are what pushed Fulani herders into banditry. We were never criminals before,” a bandit leader named Babangida said. Banditry traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders. The conflict has spiralled from raids and revenge attacks into broader, complex criminality by gangs numbering from around a dozen to well into the hundreds. They have created a kidnapping economy that raises hundreds of thousands of dollars, and at times entered alliances with Nigerian jihadists. After months of negotiation, Babangida agreed to an interview in a remote Katsina state village, following the intervention of a former government peace negotiator. “Justice is the only way out. When justice is upheld, everyone will live in peace,” said the bandit, who asked only to be identified by his first name. In the meantime, violence reigns: last week, in neighbouring Zamfara state, bandits set fire to a home during a raid, killing a family of 12. Earlier this month, gunmen killed eight police officers, and in September, more than 80 people, mostly women, were kidnapped in Zamfara and Niger states — many while working their fields. Worsening insecurity has become a major issue in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. – Corruption – Clad in a blue kaftan, the 38-year-old passes for a normal villager, save for the Kalashnikov rifle in his hand. “No bandit just picked up a gun overnight and turned to violence. There is always a story behind it,” said Babangida, sheltering from the scorching heat under a neem tree. Babangida said he turned to banditry a decade ago after his family’s 97 cows were seized by a team of police and vigilantes. He described the raid as based on indiscriminate suspicions that all Fulani are bandits. He was forced to pay millions of naira (thousands of dollars) to post bail for his mother and brother. He only recovered 10 cattle, which he used “to buy guns, one of which I’m holding now” and moved his family to a camp in the bush. Fulani herders have for generations practiced semi-nomadic herding, moving from the arid north in the dry season to the more fertile Middle Belt and southern regions, through long-established grazing routes. Desertification caused by overgrazing, the expansion of farms, climate change, population growth, and the chopping down of forests for firewood have pushed farmers and herders into contact — including instances where herds move through farmland, eating crops and destroying fields. Meanwhile, local officials, including village chiefs, police, and the military, have done little to stop farmers from encroaching into grazing areas — and in some cases, colluded with them. – Discrimination – Both farmers and herders have suffered, with attacks on farming settlements sometimes leaving scores dead. Fulanis say they face marginalisation and discrimination at the hands of the government and security forces. When cows damage fields, “the village chief will set the fine well beyond the value of the crops destroyed,” Babangida said. “But when a farmer kills a herder’s cattle, it is declared the herder’s fault and he receives no compensation,” he added. “If the chief calls the police, they will connive with a judge to raise the fine even more.” – ‘He’s right’ – The Nigerian military routinely refers to bandits as “terrorists”, and runs a dedicated military campaign in the northwest to combat them. But, addressing Babangida’s claims of “injustice”, the Katsina state internal security commissioner told AFP: “He’s right… You can’t divorce that factor (from the) drivers of this criminality”. Nasiru Muazu told AFP his state has made efforts to initiate peace dialogues and solve underlying issues driving criminality, arguing “what is happening here in the northwest is a community-driven crisis,” unlike the jihadist conflict in northeast Nigeria. “It is a serious problem” trying to balance a firm response from security forces and local diplomacy, he added. – ‘Money’ and ‘revenge’ – Some bandit gangs, driven by economic motivations in the impoverished countryside, have become massive concerns, imposing “taxes” on farmers in areas all but abandoned by the state. The military often turns to air strikes to try to rein in bandit groups in areas outside its control. Vigilante groups — repeatedly accused of extra-judicial killings by herders — have formed among farmers. Peace deals have been repeatedly struck, only to collapse. Violence has swelled in recent years. – New generation – But even Babangida is worried about the change among his criminal circle, as older bandits are replaced by a younger — and more violent, he said — generation. He blamed young bandits — often under the influence of drugs, he said — for indiscriminate violence, including killing captives after ransoms were paid. Analysts have expressed concern over alliances between bandits, who have no ideological leaning, with Nigerian jihadists. Babangida admitted that some bandits align with jihadists for strategic reasons, but maintained that for most of his comrades “it is all about making money — and revenge.” The post ‘Years of injustice’ fuel northern Nigeria violence, says bandit leader appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: INEC warns Okada riders against political violence in Oyo
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has warned commercial motorcycle and tricycle operators in Oyo State against allowing politicians to use them as instruments of violence, thuggery and electoral malpractice ahead of the 2027 general elections. The commission urged members of transport unions to resist attempts to involve them in activities capable of undermining public peace and the credibility of the electoral process before, during and after the elections. The Oyo State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Adeniran Tella, gave the warning on Thursday at the 2026 Day celebration of the Amalgamated Commercial Tricycle and Motorcycle Owners, Repairs and Riders Association of Nigeria (ACOMORAN), held alongside the launch of a book authored by the union’s chairman, Solomon Olugbode, at the Obafemi Awolowo Stadium, Oke-Ado, Ibadan. Tella, who was represented by the Head of INEC’s Information Unit, Olayiwola Awolowo, also urged members of the association to encourage their passengers and other members of the public to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). He stressed the importance of civic participation in the electoral process, saying commercial transport operators had a responsibility to protect democracy rather than allow themselves to be recruited into activities capable of threatening national security. “Let me be clear, do not allow yourselves to be used as instruments of violence or thuggery. The Nigeria Police Force has warned that the law will take its full course against anyone, no matter their status, who threatens public peace or engages in criminal conduct before, during or after the elections,” he said. Specifically, he charged ACOMORAN members to shun political violence, warning them against transporting weapons, money for vote-buying or individuals intending to disrupt the elections. “Your motorcycle or tricycle is a tool of livelihood, not a weapon of destruction. I urge you to remain politically neutral as a union,” he added. The INEC representative also cautioned the association against allowing its structures and operational resources to be deployed in support of any political party, noting that members retained the right to support candidates of their choice in their individual capacities. “While you have the right to support any candidate of your choice as individuals, the union’s infrastructure must never be hijacked to favour one party over another,” he said. He urged the transport operators to support INEC’s election logistics by ensuring the timely and safe movement of electoral materials and personnel whenever engaged by the commission. He also called on members to serve as voter education ambassadors by promoting peace, tolerance and responsible voting at motor parks and among their passengers. Similarly, the Oyo State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Abimbola, urged commercial transport operators to embrace peaceful conduct, describing their professionalism as critical to safer roads, efficient transportation and economic growth. Abimbola, who was represented by the Officer-in-Charge of the Motor Traffic Department of the state Police Command, Chief Superintendent of Police Lawrence Kehinde, described transport operators as important stakeholders in maintaining peace and security across the state. “Peace on our roads begins with the transporter. If commercial transporters conduct themselves peacefully, our cities will be safer, our journeys will be smoother, and our economy will grow,” he said. He added that peaceful conduct was a mark of professionalism, maturity and responsibility, urging every transporter to see himself as an ambassador of peace. The police commissioner also cautioned ACOMORAN members against violence and actions capable of disrupting public order during the 2027 elections. In his remarks, a leader of the Odua People’s Congress, Adesina Akinpelu, warned the transport operators against allowing politicians or other individuals to use them to foment trouble in the state. Akinpelu commended the commercial motorcyclists for sustaining their businesses despite prevailing economic difficulties, describing their services as indispensable to millions of Nigerians who depend on them for daily transportation. “Do not be used to cause troubles. Don’t let them use you. I salute your courage in this present economy. You provide essential transportation services to millions of Nigerians. Without you, many people cannot get to their destinations,” he said. He noted that the operators played important roles in the daily activities of market women, traders, students and other members of the public. Also speaking, a Muslim cleric, Mahmud Eleshinmeta, advised members of the association to exercise discipline in their personal lives, particularly in the use of their bodies, time and financial resources. He warned against substance abuse, stressing that success and the ability to perform their duties did not depend on consuming alcohol, drugs or other intoxicating substances. The cleric urged them to spend their resources prudently and adopt responsible lifestyles. Earlier, the Oyo State Chairman of ACOMORAN, Solomon Olugbode, said the 2026 Day celebration was organised to promote discipline, responsible conduct and professionalism among members. He further stressed the importance of continuous education and enlightenment, noting that the association’s development depended on members’ commitment to discipline, unity and adherence to the law. The chairman appreciated the dignitaries, security agencies, government representatives and other stakeholders who attended the celebration, urging members to translate the messages delivered at the event into positive actions. items.title: Diabète chez l’enfant : Les parents sensibilisés sur le suivi et le traitement des tout-petits
items.description: L'Association sénégalaise de soutien aux diabétiques (Assad) a organisé, le mardi 10 novembre, à Dakar, une conférence publique pour sensibiliser et encourager des parents d’enfants diabétiques. L’objectif, est de permettre aux enfants de vivre avec leur maladie sans problème. «Diabète de l'enfant : gratuité, le programme Cdic se dévoile » est le thème de la conférence publique sur le diabète, organisée par l'Association sénégalaise de soutien aux diabétiques (Assad). « Les enfants atteints du diabète doivent pouvoir vivre leur maladie tout en ayant les mêmes chances de réussite que d’autres », a souligné les organisateurs. Pr Babacar Niang, coordonnateur du programme Changer le diabète chez les enfants (Cdic), a indiqué qu’au mois de septembre 2026, environ 1915 enfants atteints de diabète sont recensés. Ils sont répartis entre Dakar, Thiès, Diourbel, Saint-Louis, Louga, Matam, Fatick, Kaolack, Tambacounda, Ziguinchor, Kolda et Kédougou. « C’est dans ce sens que 273 professionnels de santé ont été formés, 6 camps de diabète organisés au profit de 297 enfants. Ces activités pédagogiques visent à améliorer les soins des enfants atteints de diabète », a expliqué Pr Niang. Grâce aux efforts combinés de l’État et des partenaires, la mortalité des enfants et adolescents du diabète de type1 a baissé de 6,7% en 2016 à 2,6% en 2022. Il a précisé que le programme Cdic travaille avec plusieurs partenaires publics-privés. « Nous œuvrons pour accompagner les enfants vivant avec le diabète afin de faciliter leur transition vers une prise en charge adaptée à l’âge adulte. Nous voulons que vous engagiez davantage pour faciliter votre traitement. Ne soyez plus passifs », a-t-il conseillé. Pour sa part, Baye Oumar Gueye, président de l'Association sénégalaise de soutien aux diabétiques (Assad) a regretté « la rupture de continuité des soins entre un enfant suivi au Centre national hospitalier d'enfants Albert Royer et l’hôpital Abass Ndao ». Selon lui, cette situation ne facilite pas le suivi médical. D’ailleurs, si nécessaire, il promet la tenue d’un atelier afin d’y trouver une solution. « Le malade est le plus grand perdant dans cette rupture de continuité des soins », s’est désolé M. Gueye. Cheikh Ahmet Tidiane Paye du laboratoire « Novo Nordisk », a rappelé que leur structure a mis à la disposition de l’Assad, 7 tonnes d’insuline stockées à la Pharmacie nationale d’approvisionnement (Pna). De son côté, Dr Seynabou Mbow de la Division de lutte contre les maladies non transmissibles au ministère de la Santé et de l'Hygiène publique (Mshp) a promis de sensibiliser l’autorité sur la rupture de continuité des soins de certains enfants diabétiques. Des témoignages émus ont clôturé la rencontre illustrant le combat inlassable qu’abat l’Assad. Serigne Mansour Sy CISSÉ

items.title: TGR : un déficit budgétaire de 44,1 MMDH à fin octobre
items.description: L'exécution de la loi de finances 2026, sur la base des recettes encaissées et des dépenses émises, fait ressortir un déficit du Trésor de 44,1 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) à fin octobre dernier, contre un déficit de 55,5 MMDH à la même période un an auparavant, selon la Trésorerie Générale du Royaume (TGR). Ce déficit tient compte d'un solde positif de 24 MMDH dégagé par les comptes spéciaux du Trésor (CST) et les services de l'Etat gérés de manière autonome (SEGMA), précise la TGR dans son récent Bulletin mensuel de statistiques des finances publiques (BMSFP). D'après la même source, les recettes ordinaires se sont établies à 366,9 MMDH (+7,9%), portées par l'amélioration des impôts directs de 13,6%, des droits de douane de 10,9%, des impôts indirects de 9,5% et des droits d'enregistrement et de timbre de 9,8%, conjuguée à la diminution des recettes non fiscales de 16,3%. Quant aux dépenses émises au titre du budget général, elles ont été de 491,1 MMDH à fin octobre 2026, en hausse de 6,4% en glissement annuel, en raison de l'augmentation de 10,1% des dépenses de fonctionnement, de 0,1% des dépenses d'investissement et de 1,5% des charges de la dette budgétisée. La hausse des charges de la dette budgétisée s'explique par l'augmentation de 1,3% des remboursements du principal ou amortissements et de 1,7% des intérêts de la dette. L'accroissement des remboursements du principal provient de la hausse des amortissements de la dette extérieure de 7,3 MMDH, conjuguée à la baisse des amortissements de la dette intérieure de 6,5 MMDH. La TGR fait également savoir qu'au terme des dix premiers mois de 2026, les engagements de dépenses, y compris celles non soumises au visa préalable d'engagement, se sont élevés à 728,2 MMDH, représentant un taux global d'engagement de 72% et un taux d'émission sur engagements de 89% soit les mêmes niveaux un an auparavant. Sur la base des recettes encaissées et des dépenses émises, le solde ordinaire enregistré à fin octobre dernier a été positif de plus de 23,47 MMDH contre un solde ordinaire positif de 25 MMDH un an auparavant. S'agissant des recettes des CST, elles ont atteint 181,7 MMDH, compte tenu des versements effectués à partir du chapitre des charges communes – Investissement – pour 27,9 MMDH. Les dépenses émises de ces comptes ont été de 158,5 MMDH, intégrant la part des CST au titre des remboursements, dégrèvements et restitutions fiscaux pour 6,6 MMDH. Le solde de l'ensemble des comptes spéciaux du Trésor s’élève à 23,2 MMDH. Pour ce qui est des recettes des SEGMA, elles ont été de 2,32 MMDH, en baisse de 12,6%. Les dépenses se sont chiffrées à près de 1,45 MMDH (-0,1%). À fin octobre 2026, les recettes ordinaires ont été réalisées à hauteur de 87,4% des prévisions de la loi de finances, les dépenses ordinaires ont été exécutées pour 87,7% et les dépenses d’investissement ont été émises pour 67,3%. The post TGR : un déficit budgétaire de 44,1 MMDH à fin octobre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Entrée de l’IA dans le monde du travail : Mouhamadou Lamine Dianté préconise un cadre national d’accompagnement
items.description: À l’ouverture du séminaire consacré à l’intelligence artificielle et à l’intelligence humaine en entreprise, hier, jeudi 12 novembre 2026, à Dakar, le ministre du Travail, de la Fonction publique et de la Réforme du service public a plaidé pour une démarche concertée entre l’État, le patronat et les syndicats. Il propose un cadre national pour anticiper les mutations des métiers, renforcer les compétences et garantir la protection des travailleurs. Le Sénégal doit se préparer aux transformations du monde du travail induites par l’intelligence artificielle (Ia). C’est le message porté par Mouhamadou Lamine Dianté, hier, à Dakar, à l’occasion de l’ouverture du séminaire organisé par le Conseil national du patronat (Cnp), en collaboration avec la Fondation Konrad Adenauer. Pour le ministre du Travail, de la Fonction publique et de la Réforme du service public, l’Ia n’est plus une perspective lointaine : elle transforme déjà les économies, les entreprises, les administrations et les métiers. Dès lors, l’enjeu est de savoir si le pays est suffisamment préparé pour anticiper et maîtriser cette évolution. « Le Sénégal doit être acteur de cette révolution et non spectateur de transformations décidées ailleurs », a déclaré M. Dianté, soulignant que les travailleurs sénégalais ne doivent pas être de simples consommateurs passifs de ces technologies. Dans cette perspective, il a insisté sur la nécessité de dépasser l’opposition entre l’intelligence humaine et l’intelligence artificielle. « Il ne s’agit pas de remplacer l’homme par la machine, mais de donner à l’homme les moyens de faire mieux, de décider mieux et de créer davantage de valeur », a-t-il soutenu. Plutôt que de les opposer, le ministre estime que les capacités d’analyse et d’automatisation de l’Ia doivent être mises au service de l’intelligence humaine, notamment dans les domaines du discernement, de la créativité, de l’éthique et de la responsabilité. Pour permettre aux travailleurs de mieux maîtriser ces outils et d'en tirer profit, Mouhamadou Lamine Dianté a appelé à mettre l’accent sur l’emploi et le développement des compétences. Il préconise notamment d’investir dans la formation continue, les compétences numériques et l’accompagnement des reconversions professionnelles. Cinq axes pour accompagner la transition Les jeunes, les femmes et les catégories socioprofessionnelles les plus exposées aux mutations technologiques, a-t-il souligné, doivent bénéficier d’une attention particulière. « La transition numérique ne doit pas devenir un facteur d’exclusion, mais une opportunité de création de richesse, d’emploi et de progrès social », a-t-il insisté. Pour traduire cette ambition en actions concrètes, Mouhamadou Lamine Dianté a proposé l’élaboration d’un cadre national d’anticipation et d’accompagnement de l’intelligence artificielle dans le monde du travail. Cette démarche devrait associer l’État, les organisations patronales et les centrales syndicales. Cinq priorités ont été identifiées : anticiper les mutations des métiers et des qualifications, former les travailleurs, protéger leurs droits, accompagner les entreprises et les administrations dans leurs transformations et renforcer le dialogue social. Cette proposition s’inscrit dans les orientations de la Stratégie nationale de développement (Snd) 2025-2029, qui fait de l’accélération de la révolution numérique de l’économie un objectif stratégique. Le ministre a toutefois prévenu que la modernisation ne saurait se limiter à transposer les anciennes procédures sur des plateformes numériques. Elle suppose également de repenser les organisations et de simplifier les processus. « La performance économique et la justice sociale ne sont pas deux objectifs contradictoires ; elles doivent être les deux piliers d’une même ambition nationale », a-t-il précisé, insistant sur l’anticipation, la formation, l’innovation et la concertation entre les différents acteurs. Souleymane WANE

items.title: Lutte contre le trafic illicite : La Police Nationale intercepte de l’engrais chimique et des boissons frelatées de plus de 13 millions de FCFA
items.description: Dans le cadre de la poursuite de l'exécution de l’opération WIBGA 3, une équipe du Service Régional de la Police Judiciaire (SRPJ) du Nazinon, en collaboration avec la population, a intercepté, lors d'une mission de patrouille et de surveillance aux environs du carrefour de Nyorida/Manga, deux (02) camions fourgons. En provenance d’un pays voisin, les deux véhicules empruntaient des pistes afin de contourner les postes de contrôle. Le premier véhicule transportait cent vingt (120) sacs d’engrais chimique de 50 kg chacun, et le second véhicule contenait mille (1000) paquets de boissons frelatées. La valeur totale de ces marchandises est estimée à 13.500.000 FCFA. Cette action témoigne encore une fois de la détermination des services de Police en particulier, et des forces de sécurité en général, à lutter contre les circuits frauduleux et à renforcer la sécurité des personnes et des biens. La Police Nationale réitère ses remerciements aux citoyens grâce à qui ce résultat a été atteint. Elle les invite par ailleurs à demeurer toujours vigilants autour d'eux tout en poursuivant la dénonciation des cas suspects aux numéros verts mis à leur disposition que sont les 17, 16 et 1010. La Police Nationale, une force publique au service des citoyens ! Minute.bf

items.title: Burkina : Le nombre de compatriotes rapatriés de Guinée passe à 45 406
items.description: Les opérations de rapatriement des Burkinabè affectés par les récents événements en Guinée se poursuivent. Au 12 novembre 2026, le Burkina Faso a accueilli et enregistré un total de 45 406 personnes, selon un communiqué du Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR). La dynamique de retour des compatriotes se poursuit dans de bonnes conditions. L'arrivée du cinquième convoi, les cars mobilisés par la partie malienne ainsi que les initiatives individuelles ont permis d'enregistrer, au cours de la journée du 12 novembre, 8 270 nouveaux arrivants. Le bilan global s'établit ainsi à 45 406 personnes rapatriées, dont 44 304 hommes et 1 102 femmes. Parmi ces personnes figurent également 9 852 enfants et 1 224 ressortissants d'autres nationalités. Parallèlement à l'accueil des rapatriés, les actions de solidarité se poursuivent dans les différentes régions administratives du pays. Les Comités régionaux de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR) ont ainsi mobilisé les ressources et les moyens nécessaires pour assurer le transport des ressortissants depuis le centre d'accueil de Bobo-Dioulasso vers leurs régions respectives. Le CONASUR a exprimé sa reconnaissance à l'ensemble des acteurs ayant contribué à la réussite de ces opérations. Il a également réaffirmé sa détermination à poursuivre les efforts pour garantir aux compatriotes un retour, un accueil et une prise en charge dans des conditions sécurisées et respectueuses de leur dignité humaine. Enfin, le Conseil invite les populations à maintenir leur élan de solidarité et à faire preuve de responsabilité dans le partage des informations, en privilégiant les sources et les canaux officiels. Minute.bf

items.title: Protesters block INEC chair’s vehicle in London, demand resignation
items.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan, was confronted by protesters in London on Thursday over alleged irregularities in the preliminary voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The demonstrators surrounded the vehicle conveying Amupitan outside Chatham House, where he was expected to participate in a panel discussion on Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 polls. The protesters, believed to be Nigerians living abroad, shouted insults at the INEC chairman and accused the commission of abandoning its neutrality in favour of President Bola Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress. They also demanded Amupitan’s resignation, labelling INEC a “criminal organisation” over alleged duplicate voter registrations, questionable polling units and photographs suspected to have been generated using artificial intelligence. The demonstration followed mounting criticism of the commission after images and records purportedly showing suspicious entries in the preliminary voters’ register circulated publicly. INEC had acknowledged irregularities in the registration process and announced an investigation into the affected records, further fuelling the controversy. ‘Trust me I won’t fail you’ Speaking earlier at the event, Amupitan asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude, whereas results in Anambra and Osun were declared the day after voting under his watch. items.title: Why Trump crowned the man who cost him Congress
items.description: A president repudiated by the voters can bend or he can show that he won’t. Donald Trump has chosen the second, and in doing so he has revealed something about his ultimate priorities that two chaotic years of “governing” had left unclear. Vice President JD Vance blames the Republican Party’s massive midterm election losses on the Iran war , and adds living costs, inflation, and ties with Israel. Trump concedes that “ Iran was a piece of it .” Outsiders point to corruption, the spectacle of a family growing rich in office while the country paid more for fuel and food. These accounts are not wrong. But Trump’s first act after the election suggests what administration officials have left unmentioned: voters did not reject what his administration did, but what it is . To retaliate against their verdict, Trump appointed as chief of staff perhaps the most widely reviled member of an administration that does not lack for unpopular figures: Stephen Miller . The appointment matters because Trump is not a president who governs. He presides, performs, and leaves the machinery to others. The chief of staff of such a president is not an aide. He is a kind of prime minister. Susie Wiles ran the shop. With Trump showing signs of becoming even less engaged than before, Miller could end up running the country, and he will run it as he ran his immigration crackdown: by executive command, with the law treated as an obstacle rather than a boundary. Miller is not particularly associated with the Iran debacle, high prices, or corruption. He designed no tariff and sits on no crypto board. He is Trump’s deporter-in-chief, the face of the campaign to track down and remove undocumented immigrants, and he made that campaign what it is. Miller set the quota of 3,000 arrests a day and pushed Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to seize anyone without papers, not just those with criminal records. The result was a style of policing the United States had not seen in living memory: masked agents in unmarked cars seizing people on the street without identifying themselves and without warrants. The campaign did not spare citizens: Renée Good and Alex Pretti were shot dead by federal agents in Minneapolis. Hundreds of deportees were flown to African countries they had never seen and jailed there without charge. This is the ravenous apparatus Miller built. Its zealous operator now holds the most powerful unelected office in the US. The voters had judged that infernal machine. Six in ten told exit pollsters they disapproved of ICE. Hispanic voters backed Democrats by nearly two to one. After Miller’s appointment, Senator Thom Tillis called it “the worst of all possible choices” and asked how so divisive a figure could be “the olive branch” to the new Democratic majorities, as if Trump wanted to offer one. Trump did not miss this causal logic. He acted on it. Had he wanted to promote Miller without flaunting the affront to the electorate, he could have waited a month. Instead, he made the appointment three days after the midterm rout, with the exit polls still on every screen. The timing was the message. Trump even said so: Miller, he explained, is “very good politically.” The damage to Republicans in the 2028 election is a foreseeable price. By paying it, Trump is telling the country how much the deportation rampage is worth to him: more than Congress, more than his party, more than the Hispanic voters he spent 2024 courting. Only a commitment this deep can carry a cost so glaring. The proof came the same afternoon. Shortly before the announcement, Trump had told the news program 60 Minutes that the deportation policy “might be too tough” and floated a deal with Democrats to let long-settled workers stay. Then he turned the White House over to the architect of the policy he had just disowned. There was no contradiction. The words were for the interviewer; the insult was for the voters. He conceded the diagnosis and rejected the cure, in that order. The appointment reveals the limits of Trump’s supposed “transactional” style. A transactional politician cuts his losses. He drops an asset the moment it stops paying, and Trump has dropped many: generals, lawyers, cabinet secretaries, the chiefs of staff he burned through at a rate of one per year during his first term. In purely electoral terms, Miller is an asset that has stopped paying. Elevating him is not a transaction. It is not electoral politics at all. Nor is it a calculation about the two years he has left. Trump lives in the news cycle, and on election night the news cycle was his humiliation. The voters had told him, in the plainest language a democracy possesses, what they thought of his administration. The appointment of Miller was his impulsive reply. He settled a score with the electorate—the one adversary he cannot fire, sue, or deport—in the only way he could, by showing them that their verdict had not changed him. Miller has been called “the ideological id of the MAGA movement.” Trump did not promote a strategist. He promoted the id. What, then, is Trump defending? Miller has told us. Immigration, as he sees it, imports alien cultures and belief systems, and unless deportations proceed by the millions, the country will be irrevocably transformed. He has worked to narrow birthright citizenship, the constitutional guarantee that makes anyone born in the US an American. The campaign he runs is not, at bottom, about who has broken immigration law. It is about who belongs in the US. And its message reaches far beyond the people the government can legally remove. Tens of millions of citizens are being told that their papers are in order but their claim to the country is not. Trump is not deaf. Far from repudiating an appalling policy that the public has roundly rejected, he has enthroned the architect of a violent campaign to dismantle the country’s multiracial democracy. The promotion of Miller also tells Republicans what their future is worth to him. The late Lindsey Graham warned them earlier this year: “[T]o my colleagues who believe you can convince Donald Trump that Stephen Miller is a liability for him, good luck with that.” To win in 2028, Republicans must recover the Hispanic voters who fled because of the man Trump has just made chief of staff. Trump will not be on a ballot again. They will. Good luck with that. Bill Galston of the Brookings Institution called the Miller appointment a middle finger to the American public. It is also a confession. In defeat, a man reveals what he cannot give up. Trump could, in principle, give up the war, the tariffs, even the money. He could not give up the moral depravity. It is the citadel he will defend to the end. This article was originally published on Project Syndicate and has been reproduced here with permission.
